tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendMessage
tools.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: mcp__t3-code__request_secret
tools.description: Ask for one secret per single-line card; never combine values. Open it, don't offer it. Returns one-use `secretRef`, or `delivery: "file"` a file read only in its command, e.g. `adb pair <ip:port> "$(cat <file>)"`. Asked how: call now. Sign-in link: `url`. Pasted secret for child/script: `value`. Never from an old thread.

url.description: Sign-in or setup page for the value. Shown as a button.

delivery.description: secretRef (default) for a T3 tool; file for a command.

value.description: Pasted in this thread; no card.

<summary>Agent "Emails: German catalog + locale render" finished</summary>
<note>A task-notification fires each time this agent stops with no live background children of its own. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>
<result>Emails now render in the locale stored on each send, and `<html lang>` follows it. All 43 emails tests pass, and the English snapshots are unchanged.

## Changes

All edits are under `packages/emails/`. Nothing was committed.

- **`src/messages/index.ts`**: the module-level `message` export is gone. It now exports `Translation`, `Mismatched` (the placeholder check, as specified), the `Messages` interface, and `messagesFor(locale)`. `messagesFor` caches one `Messages` per locale in a Map. The `Messages` interface uses method overloads.
- **`src/messages/de.ts`** (new): the full German catalog in catalog order, following `german-style.md`. It ends with the `Mismatched` compile-time check, and `void placeholdersMatch` is lint-clean.
- **`src/messages/catalog.ts`**: the doc comment now says English is the source and German is in `de.ts`.
- **`src/Layout.tsx`**: takes a `messages` prop and renders `<Html lang>` and `<Body lang>` from `messages.locale`. `textLayout(messages, body, reason)` takes the Messages as its first argument.
- **`src/Parts.tsx`**: `ActionRow`, `ActionsCard` and `Notices` take a `messages` prop.
- **`src/AddedToTeam.tsx`, `InvitationEmail.tsx`, `ReminderEmail.tsx`, `ResultsReadyEmail.tsx`**: each uses `messagesFor(email.locale)` for subject, HTML and text.
- **`src/render.tsx`**: no change needed, since it never called `message`.
- **`src/render.test.ts`**: fixtures gain `locale: "en"`. New tests cover German snapshots for all four templates, `lang="en"` and `lang="de"` on the document, and a legacy `StoredEmail` without `locale` decoding to English.
- **`src/messages/messages.test.ts`** (new): key parity and order, placeholder-name parity, plural-category coverage (vacuous today, since there are no plural keys), a `@ts-expect-error` proving `Mismatched` catches `{puls}`, and `messagesFor` behaviour.
- **`src/__snapshots__/render.test.ts.snap`**: 151 lines added, 0 removed. These are the German snapshots only.

## Validation

- `pnpm test packages/emails`: 2 files, 43 of 43 pass.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt packages/emails`: applied.
- `pnpm typecheck 2>&1 | grep packages/emails`: prints nothing. I also ran `tsc -b packages/emails --verbose`, which reports the emails project as up to date with its dependencies.
- `pnpm lint 2>&1 | grep -A3 packages/emails`: prints nothing. The lint run does fail in `apps/web/src/messages/locale.ts` (unbound-method), which is outside my scope.
- `pnpm format:check | grep packages/emails`: prints nothing. The remaining format issues are in `apps/web/src/messages/de.ts`, `apps/web/src/messages/messages.test.ts` and `packages/domain/src/people/Directory.test.ts`.

## Notes

- **Migration**: `packages/cloudflare/migrations/0012_locale.sql` adds `person.locale`, `person.detected_locale` and `organization.default_locale`. The Organization DO applies the migrations directory as a whole, so no registration was needed.
- **Domain `people/Directory.ts`**:
  - `PersonRecord` gains `locale` and `detectedLocale`. `DirectoryState` gains `defaultLocale`.
  - `emailLocaleOf(state, personId)` is exported.
  - `AddedToTeam` sets `locale` from `emailLocaleOf`.
  - `UpdateSettings` takes `defaultLocale`, and `SettingsUpdated` carries it.

  - `settingsView` returns `defaultLocale`.
- **Domain sign-in**: `SessionState.SignedIn`, `ActivePerson`, `Member` and `OrganizationSettings` (`people/Team.ts`) carry the new locale fields.
- **Cloudflare**:
  - `SqlDirectory.ts` loads and writes the new columns and handles `PersonLanguageSet`.
  - `Organization.ts`: the `activePerson` query reads `locale`, `detected_locale` and `default_locale`. Each Invitation, Reminder, ResultsReady and resend email sets `locale: emailLocaleOf(...)`. The helpers `localeOr`/`localeOrNull` use `Schema.is(Locale)`, with no casts.
  - `auth/DurableObjectPeople.ts`, `auth/testing.ts`, `auth/PeopleTestRoutes.ts` and `EmailTestRoutes.ts` are updated for the new fields.
- **API**:
  - `updateSettings` payload gains `defaultLocale`.
  - New `PATCH /api/me/language` endpoint (`updateOwnLanguage`).
  - Both are classified in `PrivacyRegistry.ts` as `NoResultData`.
  - Handlers are in `DirectoryHandlers.ts`.
- **Tests**:
  - Directory tests cover own-language set/clear, a plain member, a removed Person (Forbidden), the admin-only default with the kept value on omission, the settings view, and the AddedToTeam locale cases.
  - `emailLocaleOf` unit cases.
  - Stored emails without `locale` decode as `"en"`.
  - Session test in `auth/SignIn.test.ts`.
  - Two new cases in `DirectoryApi.test.ts`.
  - New `packages/cloudflare/src/SqlDirectory.test.ts` runs load/apply against the real migrations.
  - Existing fixtures and expectations updated in `Organization.test.ts`, `Editor.test.ts`, `Results.privacy.test.ts`, `deliver.test.ts` and `EmailTemplates.test.ts`.

## Validation

- `pnpm typecheck`: no errors in domain, api or cloudflare. The only remaining errors are in `apps/web/src/app/App.scene.test.ts` (2) and `App.story.test.ts` (5). These are `SignedIn` and settings fixtures missing the new fields, left for the web agent.
- `pnpm typecheck:effect`: no errors. The output lists only suggestions, which are in untouched code or pre-existing lines.
- `pnpm test packages/domain packages/api packages/cloudflare/src/auth packages/cloudflare/src/SqlDirectory.test.ts`: 17 files, 384 tests passed.
- `pnpm test packages/cloudflare/src/DirectoryApi.test.ts`: 36 passed.
- `pnpm test packages/cloudflare/src/Organization.test.ts`: 5 passed (workerd, real DO SQL).
- `pnpm test packages/cloudflare/src/EmailDelivery.test.ts`: 5 passed.
- `pnpm test:privacy`: 35 passed.
- `pnpm lint`: clean.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt packages/domain packages/api packages/cloudflare` was applied, and `oxfmt --check` on the same paths is clean.

## Notes

- **Permissions**: I did not add a `Permissions.ts` entry for `UpdateOwnLanguage`. `decide` already refuses any non-active actor, so an active Person can set their own language and nobody else's. The `Permissions` table is unchanged.
- **New Person**: a Person being added is not yet in the state, so `emailLocaleOf` falls back to the Organization default.
- **Invalid stored values**: a stored language outside `en`/`de` is read as unset, which the CHECK constraints should prevent.
- **Not touched**: `packages/cloudflare/src/Submissions.privacy.test.ts` shows as modified in git status, but I did not edit it. It belongs to another agent.
- **Fixtures outside my scope**: `infra/scripts/lighthouse-gate.ts` and `infra/tests/e2e/answer.spec.ts` have `aiProcessing` fixtures. Typecheck did not flag them, but they may need `defaultLocale` once the web side is done.
- **Not run**: the web build and the e2e tests.</result>

input.prompt:
Repo: /home/ubuntu/.t3/worktrees/surveybeat-next/t3-763448b7-1472c8de1efda79d (branch r2-109-german; do NOT commit or run git write commands). Issue #109 "German catalogs and language choice". Read AGENTS.md "Toolchain traps" (Effect 4, Foldkit, TS7, no `as` casts outside *.test.ts, `.ts` import extensions, all UI text from the catalog).

YOU OWN: apps/web/src/app/** and, if typecheck needs it, infra/scripts/lighthouse-gate.ts and infra/tests/e2e/*.ts fixtures (only to add new required fields). Do NOT edit apps/web/src/messages/** (done), apps/web/src/answer/** (must stay on the English `../messages/index.ts`), or packages/**.

## What exists already
- `apps/web/src/messages/locale.ts`: `messagesFor(locale)`, live-binding exports `message`, `pluralMessage`, `formatDate`, `currentLocale`, and `setLocale(locale)` (switches the live bindings and sets `document.documentElement.lang`). German catalog in `de.ts`. New keys: `language.label`, `language.followBrowser`, `language.en`, `language.de`, `language.saved`, `settings.defaultLanguage`, `settings.defaultLanguage.help`.
- "@surveybeat/domain": `Locale` schema (`"en" | "de"`), `browserLocale(languages: ReadonlyArray<string>)`, `resolveLocale({ person, browser, organization })`.
- API (`packages/api`, typed client in apps/web/src/app/api.ts): `GET /auth/session` SignedIn now has `locale: Locale | null`, `detectedLocale: Locale | null`, `organizationLocale: Locale`. `api.directory.updateOwnLanguage({ payload: { locale?: Locale | null; detectedLocale?: Locale } })` → 204. `api.directory.updateSettings` payload accepts `defaultLocale?: Locale`; `OrganizationSettings` (GET /organization) has `defaultLocale: Locale`.

## Tasks
1. Switch every app import of `message`/`pluralMessage`/`formatDate` from `"../messages/index.ts"` to `"../messages/locale.ts"` in apps/web/src/app/*.ts (App.ts, components.ts, directory.ts, api.ts, results.ts, resultsSummary.ts, rounds.ts, session.ts, pulses.ts). Import them by name (live bindings) — never copy them into a module-level const.
2. Model (App.ts): add `browserLocale: Schema.NullOr(Locale)` filled in `initialModel` from `navigator.languages` via `browserLocale` (guard `typeof navigator !== "undefined"`; `null` when nothing matches). Session model `SignedIn` (session.ts `SessionModel` and `SessionResult`, `runSessionCall`) carries `locale`, `detectedLocale`, `organizationLocale`. Add `languageBusy: Schema.Boolean`, `languageFailure: Schema.Option(Failure)`, `defaultLanguageBusy`, `defaultLanguageFailure` like `aiBusy`/`aiFailure`.
3. Resolve and apply: export a pure `localeOf(model: Model): Locale` = SignedIn → `resolveLocale({ person: session.locale, browser: model.browserLocale, organization: session.organizationLocale })`; any other session state → `model.browserLocale ?? "en"`. At the very top of `view`, call `setLocale(localeOf(model))` before any message is produced (comment why: the browser app has one reader; the view is a function of the model, so the language follows the model).
4. Detected language: on `GotSession` SignedIn, if `sessionResult.locale === null` and `model.browserLocale !== null` and `model.browserLocale !== sessionResult.detectedLocale`, also run a command `UpdateOwnLanguage({ detectedLocale: model.browserLocale })` (fire-and-forget result message that ignores failures except Unauthenticated → LoadSession, following the existing pattern). Do NOT store or send the language anywhere related to answering.
5. Person language select: `shellView` (directory.ts) gets a `language` argument `{ value: Locale | null; busy: boolean; failure?: Failure; onChange: (value: string) => Message }` and renders, before `signOutView`, a small panel with `selectField` (components.ts) id "language", label `message("language.label")`, options `[["", message("language.followBrowser")], ["en", message("language.en")], ["de", message("language.de")]]`, plus `problemView`. Message `LanguageChanged { value: Schema.String }` → decode "" as null, "en"/"de" via the Locale schema (ignore anything else); if busy ignore; else optimistic update of `session.locale`, `languageBusy: true`, command `UpdateOwnLanguage({ locale })`; on success `languageBusy: false` and `LoadSession()`; on failure restore previous locale is optional, set `languageFailure`. Use one command definition for both tasks 4 and 5 if clean (payload struct with optional keys), or two.
6. Organization default language (Settings screen, admin only, directory.ts `settingsScreenView`): a panel like the AI processing one with `subSectionTitle(message("settings.defaultLanguage"))`, `selectField` id "default-language" options en/de (no "follow browser"), help text `settings.defaultLanguage.help`, `problemView`. Message `DefaultLanguageChanged { value }` → command `UpdateDefaultLanguage` calling `api.directory.updateSettings({ payload: { defaultLocale } })`, on success `GetSettings()` and `LoadSession()` (organizationLocale changes), Unauthenticated → LoadSession, failure → `defaultLanguageFailure`.
7. Tests (App.scene.test.ts, App.story.test.ts — read how they are written first): fix fixtures for the new required fields (`defaultLocale: "en"` in settings, SignedIn `locale: null, detectedLocale: null, organizationLocale: "en"`, Model `browserLocale`). Add:
   - Scene test: a signed-in Person with `locale: "de"` sees the Teams screen in German (assert a few German strings from de.ts, e.g. the nav "Teams"/"Organisationseinstellungen"/"Abmelden" and the language select label "Sprache") — and `localeOf` precedence unit tests: person beats browser beats organization; signed-out uses browser then "en".
   - Scene test: Organization default "de", person null, browserLocale null → German.
   - Story/update tests: `LanguageChanged` "de" issues `UpdateOwnLanguage` with locale "de"; "" issues locale null; `GotSession` SignedIn with locale null, detectedLocale null and browserLocale "de" issues `UpdateOwnLanguage({ detectedLocale: "de" })`, and does NOT when detectedLocale already "de" or locale set; `DefaultLanguageChanged` "de" issues `UpdateDefaultLanguage`.
   - After any German scene test, make sure later tests are not affected (each view call sets the locale from its model, but reset with `setLocale("en")` in an afterEach if needed).
## Validation (repo root) — all must be clean
- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm typecheck:effect`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm exec oxfmt apps/web infra` then `pnpm format:check`.
- `pnpm test apps/web`.
- `pnpm --filter @surveybeat/web build && pnpm test apps/web/src/answer/budget.test.ts` (must pass; also confirm `grep -l Teamleitung apps/web/dist/assets/*.js` lists only app-*.js chunks, never answer-*.js or messages-*.js).
Report files changed, test counts, decisions.

Your specific checks:
- **Stale English imports:** nothing under `apps/web/src` outside `answer/**` imports `../messages/index.ts` any more.
- **Module-scope text:** I found no module-level `const x = message(...)`. `WEEKDAYS` in `pulses.ts:69` is a function, and `typeName` at `pulses.ts:54` and `dateText` at `rounds.ts:49` are functions that call `message`/`formatDate` when invoked. No `message()` calls in `update` produce visible text, and `failureMessage` is only called from views. My grep for module-scope calls was crude, so I did not fully rule out a pattern it missed.
- **`LanguageChanged` / `UpdatedOwnLanguage`:**
  - The handling is sound. `chosen` separates the select from the detect call.
  - The optimistic `session.locale` update is guarded by `languageBusy`, an unknown value is ignored, and the select is disabled while busy.
  - A failed save sets `languageFailure` and `LoadSession` restores the stored value. A failed detect is silent, as intended.
- **Detection condition** (`App.ts` ~1081): it fires only when `locale === null`, the browser locale is non-null, and it differs from `detectedLocale`. A successful choice reloads the session with a non-null locale, so there is no loop.
- **`title`:** `setLocale` runs first in `view`, so the Privacy title and `shellTitle` use the current locale.
- **Double-click / label double-toggle:** the language and default-language selects are plain `<select>`s, not checkboxes, so there is no label double-toggle. Both are disabled while busy and the reducers also guard on busy.
- **Test isolation:** both test files stub `navigator` in `beforeEach` and call `unstubAllGlobals()` and `setLocale("en")` in `afterEach`.

Findings, ranked:

1. MINOR, `App.scene.test.ts:~1210` and `App.story.test.ts`: the German tests assert real German strings ("Du bist noch in keinem Team.", "Abmelden", "Sprache"), so they are meaningful. Two gaps remain:

   - The "falls back to the Organization's default" test sets `browserLocale: null` but never covers browser-over-Organization precedence in a rendered scene. `localeOf` unit tests cover it, so this is low risk.

2. MINOR, `App.ts:1139-1150` (`LanguageChanged`): picking the value that is already selected still sends a PATCH and then reloads the session. Short-circuit when `choice === model.session.locale`.

3. MINOR, `App.ts:1158` and `:1551`: every successful language or default-language save does a full `LoadSession`, which also reloads the active route's data through `GotSession`. It works. Because the optimistic `session.locale` is overwritten by the next `GotSession`, an unrelated in-flight `LoadSession` can briefly revert the select. That is cosmetic and unlikely.

4. MINOR, `App.ts:1140` (`LanguageChanged`): `languageFailure` is cleared only on the next change, so a stale error survives an organization switch. Negligible.

5. NIT, `directory.ts` default-language select: it shows `settings.defaultLocale` with no optimistic update, so it keeps the old value until the reload. This is acceptable because the select is disabled meanwhile. A scene test of the success path would pin it down. The current scene test covers only the failure path.

Nothing in the diff touches `answer/**`, and no locale goes near submissions.</result>

Closes #109. Part of #101.

## Summary
- **Catalogs:** `de.ts` sits beside both catalogs (`apps/web/src/messages`, `packages/emails/src/messages`), typed `as const satisfies Translation`. A missing key, an extra key, or a `{placeholder}` that differs from English fails `tsc`, and the `Mismatched` check names the key. Runtime parity and plural-category tests back this up.
- **Locale-aware functions:** `messagesFor(locale)` gives `message`, `pluralMessage`, and `formatDate` with `Intl` for that locale.
  - Emails render through `messagesFor(email.locale)`, with no module state.
  - The browser app uses live bindings switched by `setLocale`, which also sets `<html lang>`.
- **Language settings:** migration 0012 adds `person.locale` (NULL means follow the browser), `person.detected_locale`, and `organization.default_locale` in the Organization DO.
  - New endpoint `PATCH /me/language` sets a Person's own language. It is classified in the PrivacyRegistry.
  - `PATCH /organization` gains `defaultLocale`, admin only.
  - The session carries `locale`, `detectedLocale`, and `organizationLocale`.
- **Resolution:** Person's setting, then browser, then Organization default (`resolveLocale`).
  - The app adds a language picker above Sign out (Same as my browser / English / Deutsch) and a default language setting in Organization settings.
  - On sign-in without a choice, the browser language is recorded once as `detected_locale`, so emails follow it.
- **Emails:** each send stores the recipient's locale when it is created (`emailLocaleOf`), so retries keep the language. `<Html lang>` and `<Body lang>` follow it. Stored sends without a locale decode as `en`.
- **Privacy:** the language is never stored with a Submission, Answer, or Participation, and never reaches the Submission Worker. A new privacy test (A10) checks that no such table has a language column.

## German wording awaits the product owner's review
Claude drafted every German string, in informal "du". Please review `apps/web/src/messages/de.ts` and `packages/emails/src/messages/de.ts`. | Round | Runde ("Runde vom 07.11.2026") |
| Lead | Teamleitung |
| Organization / Organization admin | Organisation / Organisations-Admin |
| Submission / Answer | Einsendung / Antwort |
| Action | Maßnahme |
| response rate | Rücklaufquote |
| Comment redaction | Bereinigung von Kommentaren |
| viewer (role) | "Nur lesen", with `teams.yourRole` as "Deine Rolle: {role}" to avoid a gendered noun |

- **Answer page (#110):** it stays English and keeps importing the English `index.ts`. Its critical JS is 9,673 B of 10,240 B, and no German is in the answer or messages chunks.
- **MainWorker delivery-time and unsubscribe pages (#110):** these still hard-code English.
- **German Template Question texts (#111).**

- Not run: e2e against a deployed stage.

EOF
